auction_lots.lot_summary: Steel-cased Grandmaster Chime made exclusively for the Only Watch 2019 charity sale. Patek's most complicated wristwatch (20 complications, double-faced reversible case) in a metal Patek never produces for retail. Sold for charity.
Made 1933 for American banker Henry Graves Jr. 24 complications including a chart of the night sky over New York. Held the world auction record for any watch from 1999-2014, and again 2014-2019.
Paul Newman's personal Daytona, gifted by his wife Joanne Woodward in the late 1960s. Caseback inscribed 'DRIVE CAREFULLY ME'. The watch that defined the exotic-dial Daytona category.

This is the first of only four known examples of the reference 1518 in stainless steel and is believed to be the first one ever produced. It set a world record as the most expensive vintage Patek Philippe wristwatch ever sold at public auction.
A unique steel version of the Grande Sonnerie with a hand-guilloché blue enamel dial, sold to benefit research into Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
Verified result from The New York Watch Auction: XIV (Phillips New York), concluded 2026-06-14. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
Perpetual calendar chronograph in stainless steel. Only 4 known examples (the rest in gold). Held auction record for a wristwatch from 2016 until Patek 6300A in 2019.
A unique prototype from the personal collection of Francis Ford Coppola, featuring an articulated automaton hand that indicates the hours with its fingers.

An extraordinarily rare dual-crown world time wristwatch featuring a polychrome cloisonné enamel dial depicting the map of South America. It is one of only two known examples with this specific dial configuration.
Two-crown world time with hand-painted cloisonné enamel North America map dial. From a series of fewer than 10 examples with map dials.
An exceptionally rare world time reference featuring a cloisonné enamel dial depicting the map of North America, one of only three known.
A legendary reference featuring a cloisonné enamel dial with a map of Eurasia, representing the 'golden age' of Patek Philippe world time watches.
The second wristwatch ever made by François-Paul Journe and the first ever sold to a client; it set a world record for any F.P. Journe and any independent watchmaker at auction.
Unique titanium-cased 5004 made for Only Watch 2013. Patek extremely rarely uses titanium.

Bespoke 8-year commission completed for the brand's 260th anniversary. 57 complications including double retrograde split-seconds chronograph + Hebrew perpetual calendar. Still holds the record for the most complicated mechanical watch ever made.

Nicknamed the "Silk Road," this previously unknown example features a cloisonné enamel dial depicting the Eurasian landmass. It established a record for any yellow gold wristwatch at the time of its sale.
The most complicated Audemars Piguet pocket watch in private hands, featuring 19 complications including a celestial sky chart, tourbillon, and grande sonnerie.
A unique grand complication in steel created for Only Watch 2015, featuring a minute repeater, tourbillon, and perpetual calendar with a blue enamel dial.
A unique horological ensemble created by F.P. Journe and THA in 1991; the master clock automatically winds and sets the accompanying tourbillon wristwatch.
Made in 170 examples for Tiffany & Co's 5th Avenue boutique, celebrating Patek-Tiffany's 170-year partnership. Lot 1 sold for charity at Phillips on the same day the model was released — 124x retail.
A unique titanium version of the Ref. 5208, featuring a minute repeater, monopusher chronograph, and instantaneous perpetual calendar.
The only known vintage white gold manual-winding Daytona ever produced, donated by collector John Goldberger to benefit the Children Action charity.
Set a world record for the most expensive watch sold in an online-only auction; features 12 complications and a hand-engraved case.

The first perpetual calendar wristwatch ever produced by Patek Philippe, originally owned by Aisin-Gioro Puyi, the last Emperor of the Qing Dynasty. This piece is one of only eight known examples of the reference 96 with a perpetual calendar complication.
A unique and historically important tonneau-shaped perpetual calendar chronograph that served as a precursor to the legendary Ref. 2499.
Early-1950s 'first series' 2499. Square pushers, applied Arabic numerals at 12. One of the most coveted modern Patek references.
Paul Newman's personal 'Big Red' Daytona, gifted by his wife and worn by the actor for over two decades.
Featured in John Mayer's 'Talking Watches' episode. Black dial 6263 'Big Red' Daytona — one of the most photographed vintage Daytonas in the modern era.
Commissioned by Sultan Qaboos of Oman, this is one of only eight known examples, featuring a baguette-cut diamond bezel and a pavé-set diamond dial with sapphire hour markers.
Verified result from The New York Watch Auction: XIV (Phillips New York), concluded 2026-06-14. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
The first wristwatch ever made with a Grande and Petite Sonnerie minute repeating movement, marking a historic milestone in independent watchmaking.
Owned by Emperor Bao Dai of Vietnam. Only known 6062 with black dial + diamond markers. One of three diamond-set 6062s known to exist.
A rare 35mm stainless steel single-button chronograph from 1927 with a sector dial, setting a significant record for the reference.
A unique prototype featuring an automaton hand to indicate hours, inspired by an idea from Francis Ford Coppola; sold for charity at Only Watch.
One of only eight pieces produced, this model features a triple-curved case crafted entirely from blue sapphire crystal and a movement suspended by braided cables.
Verified result from The New York Watch Auction: XIV (Phillips New York), concluded 2026-06-14. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
The second Resonance ever produced, part of the legendary 20-piece subscription series that defined the brand's early success.
A unique, double-dialed wristwatch handmade by George Daniels for his personal use, featuring a spring-release case and the co-axial escapement; it set a record for any British-made wristwatch.
One of only nine examples ever produced, this piece features a double escapement with two independent balance wheels linked by a differential.
Verified result from The New York Watch Auction: XIV (Phillips New York), concluded 2026-06-14. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
Set a world record for any Akrivia or Rexhep Rexhepi watch; this stainless steel AK-06 features an open-worked dial and 100-hour power reserve.
The very first subscription tourbillon (No. 1/20), representing the absolute genesis of the F.P. Journe brand.
One of only three known examples of Ref. 1563, this unique piece is distinguished by its luminous Breguet numerals and hands.

One of only three known yellow gold 6263 Daytonas with a 'Paul Newman' lemon dial and screw-down pushers. This lot set a world record for the reference at the time of sale due to its extreme rarity and exceptional condition.

auction_lots.model: Daytona 'RCO' Paul Newman Oysterquartz Concept Outdated
auction_lots.lot_summary: Exotic-dial 6263 with 'RCO' configuration (Rosso Corsa Outline). From John Goldberger collection.
One of only 10 examples produced with a black mother-of-pearl dial to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the Singaporean retailer Sincere Fine Watches.
An oversized Calatrava in steel with a two-tone dial and Breguet numerals, which sold for 16 times its pre-sale estimate.

Formerly part of the personal collection of industry legend Jean-Claude Biver, this "pink on pink" example is unique for its blued steel hour and minute hands, a custom request from the original owner.
A unique piece created for the Only Watch 2021 charity auction, this was the last unique 15202 powered by the legendary Calibre 2121 and the first AP to use Bulk Metallic Glass.

A first-generation Speedmaster from 1957 featuring the 'Broad Arrow' hands and tropical brown dial. This sale shattered previous records for Omega, highlighting the surging market for early production tool watches in original condition.
One of only two known examples of the split-seconds chronograph reference 1436 in stainless steel, manufactured in 1945.
The second example of the limited-edition Tiffany Blue Nautilus to appear at public auction, confirming the model's extreme market desirability.
Pink gold 1518 — fewer than 60 produced in pink gold (out of 281 total 1518 production). Cleanest period perpetual chronograph.
An exceptionally rare early production model from 1999, purchased in 2000, which realized five times its low estimate.
One of only 25 pieces produced in pink gold, this double-dialed masterpiece features 12 complications including a cathedral minute repeater.
A unique platinum Daytona featuring a turquoise lacquered "Stella" dial, powered by the Zenith-based caliber 4030 and manufactured circa 1998.
A unique execution of Journe's most complex regular production model, featuring a striking blue dial and stainless steel case for acoustic resonance.
A record-breaking transparent sapphire crystal tourbillon with a movement suspended by titanium cables, one of only 10 examples produced.
A unique transitional reference featuring oversized white subdials and Art Deco numerals, predating the standard Paul Newman dial configuration.
Part of the 'Nevadian Collector' sale, this pink gold Ref. 1518 from 1948 features a matching pink dial and exceptional provenance.
A monumental platinum quadruple tourbillon featuring two double tourbillons linked by a spherical differential, achieving exceptional chronometric precision.
An exceptionally rare two-tone subscription piece from the first series of the Resonance, featuring a brass movement and numbered 17 of 20.
An exceptionally rare 18k yellow gold Paul Newman Daytona with the iconic black-and-gold "JPS" livery, one of only approximately 300 gold examples produced.
Verified result from Important Watches (Christie's New York), concluded 2026-06-12. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.

An exceptionally complicated pocket watch made for King Fouad I of Egypt in 1929, featuring a carillon minute repeater and split-seconds chronograph; it set a world record for a Vacheron Constantin at the time.
A fresh-to-market first-series example in pink gold, one of only a handful known to exist in this metal and series combination.
Setting a world auction record for a vintage Audemars Piguet chronograph, this 1930s piece is one of only two known surviving examples of the manufacture's first chronograph wristwatches.
A second-series example of the iconic reference 2499, distinguished by its round chronograph pushers and tachymeter scale. This piece was consigned from the personal collection of Jean-Claude Biver.
A second-series perpetual calendar chronograph in pink gold, one of only eight known with a Wenger case.
Verified result from Rare Watches (Christie's Geneva), concluded 2026-05-12. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
A third-series Ref. 2499 featuring a rare black lacquer dial with Breguet numerals, setting a record for this specific configuration.

A rare variant of the first automatic perpetual calendar by Patek Philippe, lacking the moonphase indicator. Only a handful of these 'Senza Luna' (without moon) examples were produced, often at the specific request of clients.

Lange's most complicated watch ever. Grande/petite sonnerie, minute repeater, split-seconds rattrapante chronograph, perpetual calendar. 6 examples made — Lange repurchases the unsold ones to maintain market position.
The only split-seconds chronograph ever produced by Rolex, one of only 12 examples made and never offered for public sale.
The only known example of Ref. 1518 bearing the 'FAB. SUISSE' signature, indicating it was originally produced for the French market.
Patek made just 4 examples of 1591 in steel. Calatrava cross hour markers. One of the rarest steel Pateks in existence.
The first platinum Anniversary watch ever produced, bearing the unique serial number 00, sold to benefit the George Daniels Educational Trust and other horological societies.

Created to celebrate the 35th anniversary of the Co-Axial escapement, this piece is one of only 35 examples. It represents the pinnacle of 20th-century independent watchmaking, hand-finished to the standards of the Daniels Method.
A unique piece created for the 10th edition of Only Watch, featuring a Faraday cage for magnetism resistance and a stainless steel case by Jean-Pierre Hagmann.
A unique prototype worn by F1 driver Charles Leclerc, sold during the Only Watch 2021 charity auction to benefit research into Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
A historically significant pocket watch manufactured in 1898, it is the earliest known Patek Philippe grand complication.

One of the original watches worn by Steve McQueen during the filming of 'Le Mans'. It was gifted by McQueen to his personal mechanic, Haig Alltounian, and remains one of the most culturally significant Heuer chronographs in existence.
One of six Heuer Monacos worn by Steve McQueen during the filming of the 1971 movie 'Le Mans', gifted by the actor to his personal mechanic Haig Alltounian.
Full sapphire-crystal case (~1000 hours of machining per case). 10 made. Movement cabled-suspended.
An exceptionally rare pink gold example from 1951, featuring the first-series dial with square chronograph pushers.
A unique prototype hand-painted in the colors of Charles Leclerc's flag, sold at the Only Watch charity auction.
Owned and customized by Gérald Genta himself, this unique Reference 5402 features an 18k yellow gold bezel he added in his own workshop.
A rare 'Tourbillon Nouveau' featuring an intricately hand-engraved pink gold dial, setting a record for the TN reference.

A triple calendar moonphase featuring a rare black lacquer dial with pyramid indexes. Unlike the 'Stelline', this configuration is exceptionally scarce, representing the peak of Rolex's mid-century dress watch complications.
The first production example of a limited series of 11 pieces, this watch was a collaboration between Greubel Forsey, Philippe Dufour, and Michel Boulanger to preserve traditional watchmaking skills.
The only known example of the Duality to be delivered with two distinct dial and hand sets, including a lacquered Roman numeral dial.
One of only three known examples of the reference 1579 cased in platinum. This piece features unique blue enamel graphics and the reference's signature faceted "spider" lugs.
Verified result from The New York Watch Auction: XIV (Phillips New York), concluded 2026-06-14. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
A world auction record for the model, this 1990 example features the 'JC' mark for Jacques Cartier and original London hallmarks, representing the pinnacle of Cartier London's avant-garde design.
Known as the 'Pink Watch,' this ultra-shock-resistant tourbillon was engineered to withstand 10,000 Gs of acceleration for professional golf.
Verified result from The New York Watch Auction: XIV (Phillips New York), concluded 2026-06-14. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
Worn by Marlon Brando in 'Apocalypse Now', featuring a hand-engraved 'M. Brando' signature on the caseback and missing its bezel.
One of only 12 examples ever produced, this oversized 44mm split-seconds chronograph is among the rarest and most complicated Rolex watches.
Formerly in the collection of Gordon Bethune, this pink gold 'Stelline' features star hour markers and is noted for its exceptional preservation.

Created to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the partnership between Richard Mille and Rafael Nadal, this limited edition of 50 pieces features a revolutionary cable-suspended movement capable of withstanding 12,000 Gs.
A grand complication prototype with 18 functions, including a minute repeater and tourbillon, developed specifically for the Only Watch charity auction.
Verified result from The New York Watch Auction: XIV (Phillips New York), concluded 2026-06-14. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
Formerly owned by Elvis Presley, this diamond-set watch was a gift from RCA Records in 1961 to commemorate his sale of 75 million records and features a Tiffany & Co. signed dial.
Limited platinum 3940 made for Patek's 150th anniversary. Standard 3940 trades in the $80k-$120k range.
150th-anniversary Patek (1989). Mini repeater + perpetual calendar + moon phase. ~50 made in platinum.
Verified result from The New York Watch Auction: XIV (Phillips New York), concluded 2026-06-14. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.

The first wristwatch to feature a dual escapement with a differential system. Only nine examples were ever produced, as the complexity of regulating two balances proved too time-consuming even for Dufour.
A complete set of five ruthenium-dial models from the private collection of Michael Schumacher, sold in their original personalized presentation box.
One of only four special-edition watches created in 2006 to celebrate the reopening of Patek Philippe's Geneva Salons, featuring a salmon dial.
Features a cloisonné enamel dial depicting a coiled dragon by master enameller Nelly Richard; believed to exist in fewer than ten examples across all Rolex references.
Verified result from The Heat Wave (Marteau & Co Online/Geneva), concluded 2026-06-17. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
A prototype of the world's first practical waterproof wristwatch, famously worn by British endurance swimmer Mercedes Gleitze during her 1927 swim across the English Channel.
A rare gem-set Daytona featuring a pavé diamond dial and brilliant-cut diamond bezel, reportedly purchased by Rolex for their museum.
Prototype to test the Trieste bathyscaphe dive to the Mariana Trench (1960). Only 7 known.
A rare 'Oyster Sotto' Paul Newman Daytona where the 'Oyster' text appears below 'Cosmograph' on the dial.
A unique piece gifted to Michael Schumacher by Jean Todt to celebrate his seven F1 World Championships, featuring a bespoke red dial with racing symbols.
A limited 'Rosso Corsa' edition with a Ferrari-red dial and Giallo Moderna hands, celebrating the collaboration between François-Paul Journe and Jean Todt.
A collaboration with Pharrell Williams featuring a hand-engraved astronaut helmet dial with a grand feu enamel reflection of Earth as seen from Mars.
Verified result from Rare Watches (Christie's Geneva), concluded 2026-05-12. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
An early subscription flyback chronograph with a brass movement and pink gold dial, setting a world auction record for the model.
A rare triple calendar moonphase with star-shaped 'Stelline' numerals, notable for its unique dark oxidized patina on the gold case.
Created for the brand's 250th anniversary, this was the world's most complicated wristwatch at the time of its release, featuring 16 complications and 834 components.
This 18k yellow gold pump-pusher Daytona with a black Paul Newman dial set a record for the most expensive watch ever sold in an online-only auction at the time.
An exceedingly rare early example with a rhodium-plated brass movement and pink gold dial, predating the official 'Souscription' series.
One of 20 'Souscription' Journe tourbillons made in 1999 with brass movements (later production used gold). The piece that established F.P. Journe at the top of independent watchmaking auctions.
A 34mm execution of the Simplicity, widely considered the finest hand-finished time-only watch in the world. This example features the movement number 57 and the signature guilloché dial.

An original 1967 London-hallmarked Crash, the most coveted iteration of the surrealist design. This example achieved a record price for the model, driven by the provenance of the London workshop and its untouched aesthetic.
An exceptionally rare Art Deco minute repeater entered into Cartier's registers in 1929; it was the only known minute repeating watch made by Cartier during that era at the time of sale.
Original 1967 London-produced Crash — Cartier's most iconic 20th-century design. Fewer than 10 known examples from the original London Crash run.
A personal gift from François-Paul Journe to his mentor George Daniels, featuring a unique dedication engraved on the movement bridge.
Part of the original 20-piece subscription series that launched the brand, previously owned by Parisian jeweler Lorenz Baümer.
1950s perpetual calendar in pink gold. ~600 produced across all variants. Predecessor to 3940 and 5140 lineages.
Owned and screen-worn by Steve McQueen during the filming of the 1971 movie 'Le Mans', this is the only example known to be fitted on a steel bracelet.
12 complications including double-faced display with tourbillon, perpetual calendar, sidereal time, sky chart. Successor model 6002G traded at $1.7M+ retail.
A historically significant prototype from 1947, this is the only known example of the first tourbillon wristwatch movement ever created by Omega for observatory trials.
Formerly in the collection of Sir Eric Clapton, one of only four known examples with a monochromatic silver dial and subdials.
Movement-suspension via PEEK/steel cable network — designed to withstand 12,000G of shock during tennis play. 50 pieces total.
Verified result from The New York Watch Auction: XIV (Phillips New York), concluded 2026-06-14. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
An exceptional ultra-flat limited edition wristwatch created in partnership with Ferrari, measuring just 1.75mm in thickness.
Hong Kong-market 3939 (the H denotes Hong Kong delivery). Tourbillon + minute repeater. ~50 made.
A rare white-gold example of the fusée-and-chain tourbillon, preserved by its original owner and featuring a deep blue dial.
An extremely rare pre-production model from 1999, predating the official brand launch; one of approximately ten examples featuring a 38mm case and white gold dial.
A yellow gold example of the first Daytona reference, consigned directly from the family of the original owner after sitting in a drawer for over 45 years.
Verified result from Rare Watches (Christie's Geneva), concluded 2026-05-12. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
The first platinum-cased RRCC1 to appear at auction, numbered 3 of 25, setting a world record for the model at the time of sale.
A rare 'Tourbillon Nouveau' model featuring a solid jade hardstone dial and a full platinum bracelet.
One of only four platinum examples produced, this piece bears serial number 01 and was sold at the Geneva Watch Auction: XVIII.
A rare white quartz carbon TPT skeletonized tourbillon featuring the iconic skull design with diamond-set teeth.
A highly rare third-generation tourbillon featuring a dial crafted from a single slice of genuine green jade gemstone.
An early tourbillon featuring a rare pink gold dial, marking the transition period before the introduction of gold movements.
A unique titanium single-button chronograph tourbillon; this historical piece was the first model created under the Akrivia brand.
1972 A-series Royal Oak — first 1000 examples ever made. Designed by Gérald Genta in a single night.
The personal watch of golf legend Jack Nicklaus, worn daily for 50 years and present for 12 of his 18 major championship wins.
A rare stainless steel chronograph featuring a possibly unique dial and the iconic 'Tasti Tondi' round pushers.
A landmark prototype of the first sapphire-cased Richard Mille, featuring one of the brand's most complicated movements.

An extremely rare oversized (36.5mm) chronograph in stainless steel. While the 130 was the standard, the 530 offered a modern presence that makes it one of the most sought-after vintage Patek sport-dress hybrids.
A rare platinum example of the self-winding minute repeater, notable for being accompanied by three different dials as confirmed by the Extract from the Archives.
A unique skeletonized tourbillon with white Agate wheels, created to commemorate the 150th anniversary of Boucheron.
Verified result from The New York Watch Auction: XIV (Phillips New York), concluded 2026-06-14. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
A rare white gold example of the first self-winding perpetual calendar wristwatch, featuring an integrated white gold bracelet.
Minute repeater + tourbillon + flyback chronograph. The Supersonnerie research project's flagship — produced ~5 per year.
The first-ever split-seconds chronograph by F.P. Journe, featuring a unique movement and blue chrome dial for the Only Watch charity sale.
A rare stainless steel example of the 'Padellone' featuring diamond-set hour markers and a triple calendar moonphase complication.
Developed in collaboration with Airbus Corporate Jets, this complex timepiece features a unique vibrating alarm complication and a dual-time tourbillon.
Triple-calendar moonphase with star hour markers ('stelline'). Fewer than 100 made between 1950 and 1953.
Numbered 20/99, this piece features a ruthenium-coated solid gold dial and movement, representing the transition from brass to gold movements.
From the personal collection of Tom Brady, this 14k gold JPS Daytona was worn by the legendary quarterback during his induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame.
A special-order ceramic Grand Complication integrating a split-second chronograph, perpetual calendar, and minute repeater.
Verified result from Hong Kong Watches: Rare and Iconic Horological Legends (Bonhams Hong Kong), concluded 2026-05-31. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
A rare pulsometer-dial Daytona designed for medical professionals to measure heart rates, featuring a bright blue pulsations scale.
Awarded to Gaston Rahier for winning the Cartier Challenge (back-to-back Paris-Dakar rallies). It is one of only four known examples, featuring a unique case design inspired by the Tuareg tagelmust.
A masterpiece of British horology from the protégé of George Daniels. This Series 2 features the latest evolution of the Co-Axial escapement and Smith's signature engine-turned dial.

An early production Resonance featuring a rhodium-plated brass movement. Collectors prize these early 'brass' pieces for their historical importance before Journe switched to 18k gold movements in 2004.
One of only five pieces made to commemorate the opening of the F.P. Journe boutique in Beijing, featuring a red dial with five stars.
A first-series subscription Resonance with a unique two-tone case, formerly in the collection of jeweler Lorenz Baümer.
The first Daytona to break the $1 million mark, featuring the 'Oyster Sotto' dial configuration where 'Oyster' appears below 'Cosmograph'.
A world record for any Submariner at the time, this lot features an exceptionally rare 'Explorer' 3-6-9 dial with the depth rating printed in red.
Numbered 14 of 50, this ultra-lightweight tourbillon weighs just 19 grams including the strap and features a movement suspended by four braided steel cables.
A unique platinum perpetual calendar featuring a copper brown dial, retailed by Asprey of London and bearing case number 1.
The only known example of Ref. 2523/1 retailed and signed by Tiffany & Co., setting a record for the reference at the time of sale.
A pristine stainless steel example of the 'Padellone', setting a record for the most expensive Rolex sold at auction in Asia at the time.
Verified result from Important Watches (Christie's New York), concluded 2026-06-12. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
A highly coveted limited edition of 50 pieces featuring a fusée-and-chain transmission and tourbillon, representing the pinnacle of the brand's 1990s revival.
An 'armored' watch designed for professional polo, featuring a tilted dual-display layout to protect the tourbillon movement from high-impact mallet strikes.
An extremely rare monochromatic "Albino" dial with white subsidiary registers and no "Daytona" signature, documented in Pucci Papaleo's '150 Steel Chronographs'.
One of the final 50 examples produced in stainless steel, featuring the Lemania-based caliber CH 27-70 Q.
A rare stainless steel Paul Newman Daytona with subsidiary dials that have aged to a uniform and highly desirable "tropical" brown color.
A 34mm white gold example with a silvered guilloché dial, movement number 167, achieving a then-record price for the model at Sotheby's.
Notable as the first wristwatch to combine a tourbillon with a progressive power reserve indicator, achieving a significant result in the May 2026 Geneva sale.
The first example of the Chronomètre Contemporain RRCC01 to appear at public auction; this 'like-new' piece is numbered 20 of a limited edition of 25.

The first model released under Rexhep Rexhepi's own name within the Akrivia atelier. This platinum example with a black grand feu enamel dial represents the modern peak of independent neo-classical watchmaking.
The very first example of the Chronomètre Contemporain II, featuring a unique layered grand feu enamel dial and a platinum case by Jean-Pierre Hagmann.

auction_lots.reference: Le Garde Temps Naissance d'Une Montre Project
auction_lots.lot_summary: Number 9 of 11 pieces from the project led by Greubel Forsey and Philippe Dufour to preserve traditional hand-watchmaking techniques.
A highly attractive gold Paul Newman Daytona with a distinctive 'Lemon' grené dial and white graphics in the sub-dials.
The first of the four unique platinum Zenith-era Daytonas to appear at auction, featuring a black Tahitian mother-of-pearl dial.
Commissioned by the Sultan of Oman, this lot features the Sultan's signature (Khanjar) on the dial and was sold by Asprey.
A 37mm example of the legendary time-only watch, showcasing Dufour's world-renowned hand-finishing and movement architecture.
A rare and elusive model launched in 2021, this flyback chronograph features a high-tech ATZ ceramic bezel and was reserved for the brand's most important collectors.
This limited edition of only 10 pieces for the American market features a red Quartz TPT case and a honeycomb movement plate made of titanium aluminide.
An extremely rare medical-themed Daytona featuring a pulsations scale on the outer track of the dial.
A yellow gold Millennium watch bearing the serial number 00, part of a series of 48 pieces created to celebrate the commercial launch of the co-axial escapement.
Minute repeater + monopusher chronograph + instantaneous perpetual calendar. ~10/year produced.
An early production example in the rarest case material, platinum, featuring a silver guilloché dial and manual-wind movement.

The very first four-minute tourbillon ever created by Abraham-Louis Breguet. It features a fan-shaped power reserve indicator and was sold to Count Potocki in 1809, making it a foundational piece of horological history.
A supremely rare and highly coveted London-made Crash model from 1990, featuring the iconic asymmetrical case and original 'Crash' deployant clasp.
A rare 18k yellow gold reference 6264 featuring the highly coveted "Lemon" Paul Newman dial with white graphics on a yellow background.
A unique piece created for Only Watch 2021, featuring a Vantablack dial and a three-dimensional movement with a cylindrical hairspring developed in collaboration with MB&F.
Number 9 of a limited edition of 35 pieces, this yellow gold Anniversary watch was offered by the original owner at the New York Watch Auction: SEVEN.
An extremely rare 20th-anniversary limited edition in platinum, distinguished by its unique blue 'Tuscan' textured dial.
The only known and correct example of a reference 6263 Paul Newman Panda retailed and signed by Tiffany & Co.
One of only 12 examples known, this oversized split-seconds chronograph from the Mondani Collection set a long-standing world record for a Rolex at auction.

A rare 6241 Paul Newman Daytona featuring the 'Daytona' text in red (Cherry) above the 6 o'clock subdial. The contrast against the gold case and black acrylic bezel makes this one of the most visually striking vintage Rolexes.
Produced in 1999 to celebrate the acceptance of the Co-Axial escapement by the industry. It uses a modified Omega movement, finished and cased by Daniels himself.
Limited to 99 pieces, this model features the automatic calibre 1300 and a ruthenium-coated dial, a hallmark of Journe's early 2000s limited series.
A 37mm rose gold example with a grey guilloché dial, showcasing the subtle aesthetic variations in the Simplicity line.
An extremely fine and rare platinum version of the reference 3974, which was Patek Philippe's most complicated wristwatch at the time of its launch in 1989.
A highly well-preserved example of the world's first serially produced perpetual calendar chronograph, featuring a rare pink gold case and matching link bracelet.
This lot set a world record for the reference in pink gold at the time; it was the first example of its kind to appear at auction with a black dial.
A rare combination of tantalum and platinum in an openworked perpetual calendar, part of a limited series of only 16 pieces.
A previously unknown and unique platinum example of the iconic square-shaped 'Cioccolatone' with a brushed case finish.
An early production example from 2001 featuring the coveted rhodium-plated brass movement and a 38mm case.

auction_lots.model: RM022 Red Quartz TPT Tourbillon Aerodyne
auction_lots.lot_summary: Verified result from Watches Online: The New York Edit (Christie's New York), concluded 2026-06-17. Reported by the MostExpensiveWatches auction desk with primary sources on file.
One of only 51 pieces produced, this masterpiece combines a tourbillon with a fusée-and-chain mechanism and a split-seconds chronograph.
A rare 1992 reinterpretation of the 1936 design, featuring a white gold case and blue numerals, produced in a highly limited run of only three examples.
Diamond-set baguette rainbow bezel Daytona, owned by Emanuel Pucci. Strong modern reference at the $700k-$900k tier.

auction_lots.model: 1815 Chronograph “2022 Best of Show, Concorso d'Eleganza Villa d'Este”
